root_cause: The TinyLlama INT8-GPU accuracy test attempts to call huggingface_hub.HfApi.list_repo_files() (via optimum's TasksManager.get_model_files), which issues an httpx GET request to the Hugging Face Hub API. The underlying httpcore/httpx connection failed with 'Name or service not known', a DNS resolution failure, before any HTTP response was received. The job only configures HTTP(S)_PROXY/NO_PROXY env vars at the Docker-container-create step (visible early in the log) but the pytest test-execution step's env block does not show the proxy variables being forwarded, strongly suggesting the proxy/DNS configuration was not propagated into the venv/python process used for the pytest run, causing outbound DNS lookups for huggingface.co (or its CDN) to fail. Other parallel accuracy tests in the same run (INT4-GPU, Qwen2 INT8/INT4) passed because their target models were already available in the local HF cache (/mnt/caches/huggingface) and did not need to reach out to the network, while the TinyLlama INT8 variant triggered a fresh metadata lookup that required network access.
reproduction_steps: 1. Run `tests/llm/accuracy_conformance.py::test_accuracy_conformance[TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0-INT8-GPU]` in an environment without HF_HUB_CACHE pre-populated for this model/quantization, or with the Intel corporate proxy variables unset in the shell executing pytest, to reproduce the DNS failure when huggingface_hub.HfApi.list_repo_files() is called. 2. Alternatively, directly run `python3 -c "from huggingface_hub import HfApi; HfApi().list_repo_files('TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0')"` without proxy env vars set, to reproduce 'Name or service not known'.
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed GPU accuracy job; this is very likely a transient infrastructure DNS/proxy issue, not a code defect introduced by the PR (which only bumps a GitHub Action version and does not touch tests/llm/*).

Verify that the pytest step for `LLM accuracy GPU tests` inherits HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/NO_PROXY from the job environment (the docker container create step sets them, but the later pytest `env:` block in the log does not list them) so that huggingface_hub calls can resolve external hosts through the Intel proxy.
Consider pre-caching all accuracy_conformance model variants (including TinyLlama INT8) in /mnt/caches/huggingface so list_repo_files() network calls are avoided entirely during CI.
Add retry/backoff around huggingface_hub network calls in tests/llm/accuracy_conformance.py (or configure HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 with pre-fetched models) to make the test resilient to transient DNS blips.
prevention_strategies: Ensure CI runner containers that need external network access (HuggingFace Hub, PyPI, etc.) consistently propagate proxy and DNS configuration into every step's shell environment, not only at container-create time. Pre-warm the HuggingFace cache for all models used by tests/llm/accuracy_conformance.py in a dedicated setup step so test execution does not depend on live Hub API availability. Consider wrapping HF Hub metadata calls with retries and clear 'infrastructure/network' failure classification in the test itself so flaky network dips do not require a full re-investigation.
historical_context: Several prior Network-category failures exist for DNS/proxy resolution against proxy-dmz.intel.com and other external hosts (e.g. patterns 4af26ac5e3256c5f 'GPU RoPE Tests fail - proxy-dmz.intel.com not resolvable', 2e6aac1671dde42f 'LLM accuracy iGPU tests fail installing requirements - Could not resolve proxy', 688d70acdbdfc8ce/dfd265b1c0ea3af5 'NPU Models Tests fail downloading external model artifacts due to DNS resolution failure'), confirming this class of transient network/DNS failure recurs periodically across different jobs that need external connectivity. This is the first occurrence of the specific httpx ConnectError signature during huggingface_hub.list_repo_files for the TinyLlama GPU accuracy test.
